The relevant skill, alpha-hypothesis-writer, enforces a 'mechanism-anchor gate': a hypothesis may only be emitted if it is anchored to real panel columns (1.0 ANCHORED dispatches, 0<c<1 PARTIAL dispatches flagged, 0.0 UNANCHORED is BLOCKED), plus an eight-fingerprint pre-registration committed BEFORE any backtest runs, horizon clamping against the holdout, and event clustering so that one event cluster yields one spec with tests_independent = SUM rather than max. candidates.what_it_would_replace_or_improve_in_our_: Its PRE-REGISTRATION GATE is the idea our package most conspicuously lacks in one place. Our intake gate (leapspace/backtest.py::apply_intake_gate) already refuses a spec whose parameters lack parameter_provenance - that IS a pre-registration gate and it is stronger than this one. But the MECHANISM-ANCHOR rule and the CLUSTERING rule are new: our 13 specs would benefit from an assertion that every claimed mechanism is backed by a real column in the data and that correlated event clusters are not counted as independent tests. Our edge.py already handles the independent-bet side of this for wallets; this would do it for SPECS.

candidates.name: tradermonty/claude-trading-skills (data-quality-checker only, scored separately)
candidates.what_it_does: The single most directly transferable candidate in this whole comparison, and it is scored separately because it is a genuinely self-contained unit. Five check families over a markdown report: price_scale (ETF vs futures price-scale inconsistency), notation (instrument symbol errors), dates (date/day-of-week mismatches with year inference), allocations (allocation totals that do not sum), units (unit mismatches). 26,136-char stdlib-only script with a Finding dataclass, a markdown report generator and a pytest suite under scripts/tests/. Advisory mode: flags issues as warnings for human review, never blocks. Supports English and Japanese content.
candidates.dependencies: Python 3.9+, STANDARD LIBRARY ONLY, no third-party packages, no API key. Ships its own pytest suite.
candidates.license_notes: MIT LICENSE in the repo root (same repo as the entry above).
candidates.what_it_would_replace_or_improve_in_our_: This is the single highest-value, lowest-risk adoption. Our package has a RULE that any price comparison across time must pin the venue (it found and fixed a +30,833% cross-pool artefact) and a rule that the PRODUCER and CONSUMER of a snapshot must share the selection rule (it found a base-selection drift that emptied the NICHE bucket and still printed a confident verdict). Both were caught by hand. A mechanical pre-flight validator over the rendered report would catch the whole family automatically - including the allocation-sum and date-weekday checks that we do not do at all, and it composes with our existing leapspace/tests/check_report_integrity.py, which asserts the report matches the data but does not check the report's INTERNAL arithmetic.
candidates.risk_or_drawback: It checks MARKDOWN documents, not JSON payloads or on-chain tables, so it covers our report renderer but not our chain/h-holder artefacts. It is a text scanner: it will need extending to our specific number formats (USD with commas, our provenance strings) before it is worth running in CI. Advisory-only by design, so it will not block a bad report on its own - someone must make the warnings matter.
